1 1. Brief facts of the case, relevant for the disposal of the present suit are that the plaintiff has filed the present suit seeking compensation for Rs.10,00,000/- from the defendants. Plaintiff submits that defendant no.1 is responsible for over all supervision and control on production, storage and transmission of electricity in Delhi and defendant no.2 has become the successor of Delhi Vidyut Board in respect of the responsibility, control and management of transmission of electricity and responsible for maintenance, control and transfer of electricity including one where the cause of action for filing the present suit arose. 
2. It is averred that plaintiff is working as Project Engineer with A2Z Engineering & Maintenance Services Limited at Karnal Haryana and is getting salary of Rs.11,250/- per month and is only son of his parents. Plaintiff got his very first job with defendant no.2 as GIS Engineer in July 2008 with a salary of Rs.9,000/- per month. On 18.11.2009 plaintiff changed his service from BSES to A2Z Engineering & Maintenance Services Limited at Karnal Haryana as a Project Engineer with a salary of Rs.9,000/- per month + HRS and mobile phone facility. In April, 2010 his salary was increased @
Rs.11,250/- per month in place of Rs.9,000/-. On 21.03.2010 after his duty plaintiff boarded in bus coming to Delhi for picking-up his goods from his friend Mr. Somesh Shah who was residing at Sec.
27, Noida. Plaintiff took auto-rickshaw bearing no.DL1RK-3884 from Kashmiri Gate Bus Station and reached at the Red Light Signal Opposite Mayur Vihar Phase-I, Metro Station, Delhi-Noida Link Road, Mayur Vihar Phase-I, Delhi. In the meantime, suddenly an Electric Pole of High Tension wire fell on the Auto-Rikshaw bearing no.DL1RK-3884 in which the plaintiff was traveling and due to said accident, auto-rickshaw got badly damaged and burnt as electricity was passing through the High Tension Wire. The severity of the said accident is res ipsa loquitor from the fact that the auto driver Sh. Ashok Kumar died on the spot due to the said accident and plaintiff sustained serious injuries on his face, head and all over his body and became unconscious. He was taken to Jeevan Anmol Hospital by one Col. Manoj and admitted there vide MLC no. 743 dt. 22.03.2010. A FIR bearing no. 107/2010 was registered at PS Pandav Nagar. It is further averred that apart from serious and grievous injuries on his face and head, plaintiff sustained multiple fractures on his face and head and several injuries on his left knee, left forearm, left index finger. After examination, the doctors detected that plaintiff has sustained 14 fractures as well as other injuries due to the said accident. It is further averred that plaintiff was operated and remained admitted for treatment from 22.03.2020 to 01.04.2010. During operation, the plates have been inserted in forehead and jaw of the plaintiff and 62 stitches has been given to the plaintiff from forehead to eye and 65 stitches at nose and left knee and was on complete bed rest upto 21.05.2010. On 22.05.2010 the plaintiff joined his duty however, since the condition of the plaintiff was further deteriorated, the plaintiff was again advised to take complete bed rest from 26.05.2010 to 22.06.2010. Due to the unfortunate accident,
engagement ceremony fixed for 05.04.2010 could not be performed and was cancelled considering the serious condition of the plaintiff. 
3. Plaintiff further avers that the said accident was caused due to the negligent acts of the defendant no.2 who was responsible to take care and maintain its high tension wires and poles containing the said wires. Had the defendant no.2 taken care of the poles the aforesaid accident could not happened. The fall of the poles shows that the same was not properly fixed in the earth and was not inspected or checked by the defendant no.2. The defendant no.1 is also responsible for the acts of the defendant no.2 and is thus arrayed in the present suit. The defendant no.3 and 4 are the insurance Ajay Kumar vs State on 6 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35976961/
2 company of the defendant no.2 and are under obligation to compensate the person who suffered due to the negligent act of the defendant no.2 and therefore, all the defendants are jointly and severally liable to compensate the plaintiff.
4. Plaintiff incurred expenditure on treatment about Rs.3 lacs for hospitalization, operation,
medicines, Rs.1 lac approx on his extra nutrition and betterment, Rs.1 lac on taxies/ambulance and hotels. Plaintiff remained absent from his duty w.e.f. 21.03.2010 to 21.05.2010 and also from 26.05.2010 to 22.06.2010 and the said loss comes to Rs.33,750/-. Due to the said accident,
plaintiff's future has been shattered and even today, plaintiff is not working well as he is suffering pain and feels that there are two images of the one things. The plaintiff is accessing his loss toward physical pain, mental pain, suffering, future loss, loss of companion, loss of wages etc. @
Rs.4,66,250/-. It is further averred that no money can compensate the plaintiff towards the losses suffered by the plaintiff due to the said accident, however, plaintiff is restricting himself and is claiming a compensation of Rs.10 lacs against all the defendants. Hence, plaintiff has filed the present suit for compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- in his favour and against the defendants with 24%
per annum interest thereon till date of actual payment. 
5. As per record, the defendant no.1 has been proceeded exparte vide order dt. 20.09.2011 and there is no written statement of defendant no.1 on record. 
6. Written statement was filed by defendant no.2 wherein it is stated that on 21.03.2010 the report of the accident was prepared and it was found that M/s D.S. Construction Limited was carrying out the work of road widening and the fly over on Delhi-Noida Link Road opposite to Delhi Police Apartment. The company while carrying out the work had indulged in heavy excavation or a hit to the tower by the heavy machinery. The competent authority of Government of NCT of Delhi vide its letter dt. 31.03.2010 had also constituted an enquiry committee to see whether there is any negligence on the part of any agency. The said committee had given an interim report dt.
07.04.2010 and final report dt. 28.08.2010. In the final report, it was specifically held that,
"responsibility cannot be fixed to any known person or agency as the reason of collapse of towers is due to mischievous act of unknown persons.". It is averred that answering defendant carries out the routine checkups of inter alia its high tension towers and whenever any of its part including fish plates are missing, a report is also lodged with the police. In this case no police complaint was ever lodged as till the last of such inspections which was carried out periodically no fish plates were missing. The site inspections are carried out regularly and is also recorded and the last checkup was carried out in March 2010 only.
7. Defendant no.3 also filed its written statement wherein it has been submitted that answering defendant is liable to indemnify only that loss which is admitted by M/s BSES YPL subject to insurance policy is effective on claims made basis which was effective for the period 19.12.2012 to 18.12.2013 therefore, Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. is not liable to indemnify any loss to insured and to pay compensation to plaintiff and answering defendant be deleted from the array of respondents. It is further averred that there is compulsory excess clause i.e. Rs.1 lac for each and every claim. It is averred that answering defendant is having the policy contract with M/s BSES YPL and is not a direct party in relation to the claimant. The liability of the answering defendant will be Ajay Kumar vs State on 6 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35976961/
3 devalued if the negligence of BSES is proved. There is no cause of action against the answering defendant as BSES has not intimated about the happening of the alleged accident as per terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy. The competent authority of Government of NCT of Delhi vide its letter dt. 31.03.2010 had also constituted an enquiry committee to see whether there is any negligence on the part of any agency. The said committee had given an interim report dt.
07.04.2010 and final report dt. 28.08.2010. In the final report, it was specifically held that,
"responsibility cannot be fixed to any known person or agency as the reason of collapse of towers is due to mischievous act of unknown persons.". It has been submitted by answering defendant that the reason for accident was either the heavy excavation or a hit to the lower by the heavy machinery therefore, no cause of action has arisen against M/s BSES YPL and answering defendant. Thus, it is prayed that answering defendant be deleted from the array of defendants and suit of the plaintiff be dismissed with heavy cost as the same is bad for misjoinder and non- joinder of necessary and proper parties. 
8. Vide order dated 20.09.2011, the original defendant no.3 & 4 i.e. Reliance General Insurance Company and Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. were deleted from array of parties. Subsequently,
on 13.02.2018 defendant no.3 Reliance General Insurance Company and defendant no.4 M/s D.S.
Construction were impleaded in the present suit 9. Defendant no.4 also filed its written statement thereby therein that no relief was claimed by the plaintiff against the defendant no.4 in its original plaint and it was only on the basis of the allegations raised by the defendant no.2 in its written statement, that the defendant no.4 was carrying out the works of road widening, the defendant no.4 was arrayed as a party to the proceedings. It is further stated that averments contained in the written statement qua the defendant no.4 are extremely vague and misconceived as any accident/mis-happening or loss/damage to any person/property which may be arising due to any electricity pole shall be solely of the defendant no.2 whereas pleading shows that defendant no.2 has sought to shift its liability to defendant no.4 which is vague and unsubstantiated. The entire basis of the allegation is a self styled report dated 22.03.2010 made by defendant no.2 which was allegedly forwarded to the Chief Electrical Inspector, Government of NCT of Delhi. The said report neither has any basis nor any supporting document to even remotely suggest as to how the defendant no.4 is sought to be made liable for the alleged accident. It has not been provided in the report as to how and on what basis,
the defendant no.4 has sought to be made responsible. The said report evidences sheer manipulation of facts by the defendant no.2 attempting to transfer liability to the defendant no.4 which should be put to strict proof in relation to the said report as well as the pleadings founded upon it. Defendant no.2 further relied upon a letter forwarded to the concerned SHO whereas defendant no.2 has not provided any details if the letter was registered or not. The said letter appears to be another desperate attempt of the defendant no.2 to somehow attribute responsibility for the alleged incident on the defendant no.4. It is further averred that the interim inquiry report submitted by the committee formed by the Government of NCT of Delhi, no conclusion/finding was given as to the reason for the collapse of the towers. The final report had a detailed inspection of the place of the alleged accident. The authority examined the reports submitted by the PWD, BSES and even inspected the items so collected by the police which were kept in Pandav Nagar Police Station,
authority after going through the replies mentioned in its final report that, 'a bare perusal of the Ajay Kumar vs State on 6 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35976961/
4 above reply of PWD, which is based on the documentary evidence and photographs, clearly shows that no work has been done by the defendant no.4 even close to the towers since over six months and the work of boulder pitching in past was being done manually and without the use of any heavy machinery.' The said reply of PWD deliberately not been placed on record by the defendant no.2 and the said reply has not been disputed by the defendant no.2. It has been further submitted that it was the duty of the defendant no.2 to ensure that the poles are properly embedded as the same are stacked in an open public area. It was certainly the duty of the defendant no.2 to ensure that any of their acts to not cause any harm or injury to any other person. Defendant no.2 was negligent in not taking appropriate safety measures even after being well aware of the fact that the electric poles were kept stacked in public place, where general public had easy access. Thus, the liability if any,
should be attributed to the defendant no.2 for breach of duty for maintaining the electric poles,
leading to the alleged accident. It has been further submitted that the allegation of the plaintiff that the answering defendant was negligent in carrying out the work of road widening the flyover is wholly false and baseless. The answering defendant duly carried out the requisite inspection and checks, and completed the entire project with utmost care and caution and there has been no act on the part of answering defendant which has lead to any hard to the plaintiff as alleged. Thus, it has been prayed that the present suit be dismissed with heavy costs on the plaintiff. 
10. Replication to the written statement of defendant no.2 filed on behalf of plaintiff thereby reiterating and reaffirming the contents of his plaint. Plaintiff averred that defendant no.2 is trying to shift its liability on M/s D.S. Constructions Limited and defendant no.2 be directed to furnish the complete details of M/s D.S. Constructions Limited so that the plaintiff can take necessary action of impleading M/s D.S. Constructions Limited as defendant in the present suit. Plaintiff denied the final report and stated that it is the defendant no.2 who was negligent in regular monitoring of its electrical towers and poles. Rest of the contents of the written statement are denied by the plaintiff. 
11. Replication to the written statement of defendant no.4 has also been filed by plaintiff . Plaintiff averred that initially the plaintiff has not incorporated the answering defendant in the array of parties as at that time the plaintiff was unaware about the fact that the answering defendant was doing widening of road and due to the negligent act of the answering defendant, the high tension wire collapsed and the plaintiff sustained grievous injuries. It is further averred that answering defendant intentionally and deliberately trying to shift its liability on the defendant no.2. Presence of answering defendant is duly proved as he is specifically stated under para that, "the defendant no.4 carrying out road widening activities in the said area", but deliberately denying its liability and negligent act. It is submitted that the defendant no.4 has already been incorporated in the array of parties and the plaintiff has already filed amended memo of parties on record. It is averred that defendant no.2 and defendant no.4 both are shifting their burden against each other. In fact the accident has been caused due to the negligent act of the defendant no.2 and 4 and defendant no.3 being insurer of defendant no.2 is liable to pay damages to the plaintiff. 
12. Ld. Predecessor Court has framed the following issues vide its order dt. 19.02.2019:
a) Whether the suit is not maintainable as against defendant no.2 and 3 and has cause of action, if any, as against M/s D.S. Construction Limited? OPD 2 & 3.

5 b) Whether the suit is liable to be dismissed against defendant no.4 as no relief is claimed against them? OPD-4. 
c) Whether the plaintiff is entitled for recovery of a sum of Rs.10 lacs as compensation alongwith pendentelite and future interest? OPP d) Relief.

On 02.09.2019, to prove his case, plaintiff, examined himself and tendered his affidavit Ex.PW1/A, bearing his signatures, at points 'A' and 'B', also relied upon following documents:

16. Plaintiff's witnesses were duly cross-examined on behalf of defendant no.2,
defendant no.3 and defendant no.4 respectively. 
Thereafter, plaintiff's evidence was closed vide order dt. 26.02.2020.

6 17. Defendant no.2 examined Sh. R.K. Tola, Ex.-GM(T), Delhi Transco Limited as D2W1 who proved the inquiry report dt. 07.04.2010 and final report dt. 28.08.2010 Mark D2W1/A and Mark D2W1/B.
18. Defendant no.3 i.e. M/s Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. examined Sh. Dharmender Singh,
Admn. Manager, as D3W1. He got exhibited his identity card as Ex.D3W1/1. He proved the attested true copy of insurance policy as Ex.D3W1/2. In his cross-examination he submitted that defendant no.2 was insured with defendant no.3 and alleged policy was valid for the period of 19.12.2009 to 18.12.2010. As per the terms and conditions and contract of insurance between the defendant no.2 &
3, defendant no.3 is liable to pay compensation/liability to BSES YPL, if there is no violation of terms and condition and contract of insurance. He admitted that, 'our contract is with defendant no.2'. Thereafter, Ld. Counsel for defendant no.3 closed evidence on behalf of defendant no.3 on 30.05.2023.
19. Defendant no.4 examined Sh. Santosh Kumar Gupta as D4W1 who proved the board resolution dt. 03.10.2017 as Mark D4W1/1 (Ex.D4W1/1) and board resolution dt. 20.03.2023 as Ex.D4W1/2. 
In his cross-examination witness deposed that during the relevant period defendant no.4 company was executing the work of flyover, bridges etc. defendant no.4 company was not executing any work near the place of accident and we had taken all safety measures for construction work. He deposed that he was coordinating for the PWD work awarded to defendant no.4 company and was visiting site from time to time. But at the time of accident, he was not present. He denied that accident took place due to negligence of defendant no.4 company. Thereafter, evidence on behalf of defendant no.4 company was closed matter was fixed for final arguments. 
20. I have heard Ld. Counsel for the parties and have perused the material placed on record and considered the submissions. 
21. My issue-wise findings are as follows:
22. Issue no.2:
"Whether the suit is liable to be dismissed against defendant no.4 as no relief is claimed against them? OPD-4." 
22.1 The onus to prove this issue is upon defendant no.4. It is the contention of defendant no.4 that no relief was claimed by plaintiff against the defendant no.4 in his original plaint and it was only on the basis of allegations raised by defendant no.2 in its written statement, that the defendant no.4 was carrying out the works of road widening, the defendant no.4 was arrayed as a party in the present case. It is further the plea of defendant no.4 that the defendant no.2/BSES is trying to shift its liability to defendant no.4 on the basis of its self styled report dated 22.03.2010. 22.2 During the arguments, Ld. Counsel for defendant no.4 drew the attention of this Court towards the report of committee wherein clause 8.2, it is mentioned that, 'BSES has put the blame on PWD and movement of their heavy machinery in road widening work as cause of collapsing of towers. BSES could not produced structural design and drawing of towers due to the fact that these were done originally by DVB nearly 20-25 years back and are not available to them. Ld. Counsel for defendant Ajay Kumar vs State on 6 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35976961/
7 no.4 further argued that the report of committee has nowhere given any finding against the defendant no.4.
22.3 As far as the contention of Ld. Counsel for defendant no.2 that it was the duty of defendant no.4 to follow the safety norms of electricity rules is concerned, suffice is to say that the defendant no.2 is/was under the duty to get compliance of the said rules from the defendant no.4 which defendant no.2 failed to do so.
22.4 Moreover during cross-examination by Ld. Counsel for defendant no.2, PW1 deposed that, 'I cannot say whether the cause of calling of high tension tower on 21.03.2010 was due to work of road widening carried out by defendant no.4 DSC Limited or due to heavy excavation work which was done by using heavy machinery, equipments, by defendant no.4 or the cause of accident was negligence of defnedant no.2. It has further come in evidence of PW1 that he did not see any heavy machinery around the high tension electric tower. The defendant no.2 has not brought any evidence on record to prove any such casual connection between the road widening work and fall of tower. 
22.5 It may be relevant to note here that a bare perusal of the record depicts that defendant no.2 has tried to shift its liability to defendant no.2 by making only bald averments without producing any documentary proof such as photographs. However, as per the averments of defendant no.2 the site was inspected by Electricity Inspector on the date of incident and defendant no.2 had enough proofs to bring the truth on record. 
22.6 Hence, due to non filing of any supporting documents by defendant no.2, an adverse inference is drawn against the defendant no.2 that defendant no.2 has no evidence to prove its averments as regards to negligence of defendant no.4 causing the accident. 
In view of above observation, it is held that the defendant no.4 is not liable to compensate the plaintiff. The present issue is decided accordingly. 
23. Issue no.1 & 3: 
'Whether the suit is not maintainable as against defendant no.2 and 3 and has cause of action, if any, as against M/s D.S. Construction Limited? OPD 2 & 3.' & 'Whether the plaintiff is entitled for recovery of a sum of Rs.10 lacs as compensation alongwith pendentelite and future interest? OPP' Both the issues are inter-connected. 
Therefore, are being discussed together. 
23.1 The onus to prove issue no.1 is upn defendant no.2 & 3 and issue no.3 is upon the plaintiff. If the injury to the plaintiff is cause because of the negligence of the defendants, then under the law of torts, the plaintiff shall be entitled to recover compensation against the defendant. 
23.2 The onus to prove this fact was upon the plaintiff that the accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of defendant. In order to discharge, the plaintiff had Ajay Kumar vs State on 6 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35976961/
8 examined himself as PW1 and has reiterated the aforesaid averments in the plaint, in his examination-in-chief. PW2 MHC(R) of PS Pandav Nagar has proved FIR Ex.PW1/8 and PW3 who is medical record officer from Jeevan Anmol Hospital,
Mayur Vihar, has proved medical documents of plaintiff Ex.PW3/A showing that the plaintiff had suffered severe injuries in accident. 23.3 In addition to it, it may be relevant to note that the defendants have not disputed the cause of accident and defendant no.2 have in the pleadings raised accusing fingers against the defendant no.4, so far as negligence is attributable, which resulted in the fall of tower and severe injury to the plaintiff. 
23.4 In the written statement, the defendants has simplicitor denied the contention in the plaint mentioning that there was no negligence of the defendants. The defendants admitted in one way or the other the cause of accident and injury to the plaintiff as mentioned in the plaint and proved from the testimonies of PWs and report of committee Ex.D2W1/A and Ex.D2W1/B. 23.5 It may also be relevant to mention here that defendant no.2 submitted in its written statement that on 21.03.2010 the report of the accident was prepared and M/s D.S. Constructions Ltd./defendant no.4 was found to be negligent and reason for the accident. On the basis of the said report the defendant no.2 has tried to wriggle out of the negligence however, no such report has been proved by defendant no.2. 23.6 Moreover, the defendant no.2 examined D2W1 Sh. R.K. Tola who proved the reports of committee i.e. interim inquiry report dt. 07.04.2010 and final report dt. 28.08.2010 which are Ex.D2W1/A and Ex.D2W1/B. Here it is necessary to reproduced the relevant portion of the final report hereinbelow: 
"9.0 Findings After going through site inspection, all the documents, records,
photographs, seeing the material in Police Station, the committee came to the following findings:-
(i) It is established that falling of one tower has resulted in falling of other four towers simultaneously due to their connectivity with heavy High Transmission wires on top,
(ii) From the site conditions, it could be inferred that tower no.1 (end tower) was the one which fell first and in the process was the cause of falling of other four towers also,
(iii) It is also a fact that two supports of tower No.1 appear to be dislodged from their footing due to absence of connecting gusset (fish) plates, nuts & bolts. Some of these were found in Police custody (Photographs nos., 12, 13 & 14 refer). Photographs nos.
1,2,3,&4 further corroborate the theory of removal of nuts, bolts and gusset plates angles,
(iv) Presence of tools, etc. in the custody of police station also confirms that some mischief monger had tried to dislodge the stability of structural members of end tower at the connections by Ajay Kumar vs State on 6 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35976961/
9 removing the nuts & bolts/gusset (fish) plates, etc. for some petty gain, although it is difficult to comprehend this can be done with the help of those tools available in the custody of Police.
However, pattern of failure of end tower (as in photograph no.s1,2,3 &4) points toward removal of connecting gusset (fish) plates, nuts & bolts.
(v) Responsibility cannot be fixed to any known person or agency as the reason of collapse of towers is due to mischievous act of unknown persons.
(vi) Suggestions as given in the interim report of the committee and as mentioned in para no.4.2 above are to be taken a note of and be implemented urgently in order to avoid occurrence of such incident in future."
23.7 Bare reading of report of committee depicts that there was negligence on the part of defendant no.2 in as much as violation of the provision of the Electricity Act have been found to be there at the spot by the committee and the said negligence is further fortified by the fact that no record of regular site inspection and visits have been produced and proved by the defendant no.2.
24. It may be noted that being civil suit for damage, this suit is to be decided on the basis of preponderance of probabilities in as much as the facts required to be proved for obtaining a decree in the civil suit and a judgment of conviction in the criminal proceedings maybe overlapping but the standard of proof in a criminal case viz. a viz. a civil suit, indisputably is different. Whereas, in the criminal case, the prosecution is bound to prove the commission of the offence on the part of the accused beyond any reasonable doubt, however, in a civil suit, preponderance of probabilities will serve the purpose for obtaining a decree. 
25. In this regard, it may be noted that in the facts and circumstance of the case the doctrine of res ipsa loquitur would also apply with force in as much as the said maxim is based on common sense and its purpose is to do the justice when the facts bearing on the causation and on the care exercised by defendant are at the outset unknown to the plaintiff and are or ought to be within knowledge of the defendant. The plaintiff merely supposed to prove a result, not any particular act or omission producing the result. If the result in the circumstances, in which plaintiff proves it, makes it more probable than not that it was caused by the negligence of the defendant, the doctrine of res ipsa loquitur is said to apply and the plaintiff will be entitled to succeed unless the defendant by way of evidence rebuts that probability.
26. At this stage it is relevant to impute strict liability upon the defendants as the doctrine of strict liability has its origin in English Common Law when it was propounded in the celebrated case of Rylands v. Fletcher, 1868 Law Reporter (3) HL330. The rule of strict liability was approved and followed in India in several decisions and has been reiterated in the catena of judgments. The sum and substance of this principle is that due to the action or inaction of the State or its officers, the fundamental rights of a citizen are infringed then the liability of the State, its officials and its instrumental also is strict. Claims raised for compensation in such a case is not a private law claim of damages, under which the damages recoverable are large. Claim made for compensation in public law for compensating the claimants for deprivation of life and public liberty which has nothing to do Ajay Kumar vs State on 6 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35976961/
10 with a claim in a private law claim in tort in ordinary civil suit. Even if all the safety measures had been adopted, a person undertaking an activity involving hazardous or risky exposure to human life is liable under law of torts to compensate for the injury suffered by any other person, irrespective of any negligence or carelessness on the part of the Managers of such undertaking. The basis of such liability is the foreseeable risk inherent in the very nature of such activity. The liability cast on such person is known in law as strict liability and it differs from the liability which arise on account of negligence i.e. the concept of negligence comprehends that the foreseeable harm could be avoided by taking reasonable precautions . 
27. It may be noted that though not quoted, reliance is placed on M.P. Electricity Board v. Shail Kumari (2002) 2 SCC 162 and Union of India v. Prabhakaran Vijay Kumar (2008) 9 SCC 527,wherein, it was reiterated that the rule of strict liability as laid down byHon'ble Supreme Court in M.C. Mehta Case (1987) 1 SCC 395 is not subject to any exceptions as laid down in the judgment of Rylands v. Flethcher (supra) and in Shail Kumar (supra) it has been observed in para no. 8 & 12 as under :
"8. Even assuming that all such measures have been adopted, a person undertaking an activity involving hazardous or risky exposure to human life, is liable under law of torts to compensate for the injury suffered by any other person, irrespective of any negligence or carelessness on the part of the managers of such undertakings. The basis of such liability is the foreseeable risk inherent in the very nature of such activity. The liability cast on such person is known, in law, as "strict liability".
